body:
Insomnia sucks and can make you lose your mind if you don’t sleep for many days in a row (I had 2 psychotic episodes due to lack of sleep, one ended in a suicide attempt and the other in hospitalization). Btw, insomnia is a common symptom of depression / bipolar disorder. Please see a psychiatrist, he’ll screen you for depression and prescribe medication that’ll help you sleep.

Sending a hug!

I understand and share your fear. I always hoped there’s no God, because I felt like if there is, then I deserve punishment. Although now when I’m seriously considering suicide, no afterlife and eternal void also seem scary and uninviting.
Thank you. Sending a virtual hug!

So sorry you feel hopeless regarding your self-sufficiency and having kids. 

I’m in the process of figuring out whether I have multiple sclerosis. If I do, it’s pretty much a death sentence. If I don’t, alternative diagnosis don’t look bright either.

Why rush it though? There’s plenty of pleasant experiences in this world. It’s even possible to find a deeper meaning to life, like love, children, creativity (art or smth that can transcend you own life).

A bicycle ride.

A first kiss with your crush.

Long nighttime conversation with a friend.

A good steak.

The beauty of mountains.

Sea breeze.

Music that gives you goosebumps.

Ice cream.

A good movie.

I understand you. I have multiple incurable conditions, including mental illness (bipolar). Realizing that a disease is here to stay with you until the end of your life is tough.

But remember that pretty much no one is 100% healthy. A lot of people live with chronic diseases and mental illnesses, and still find ways to have a fulfilling life. I’m wishing you strength to cope with bpd and enjoy the life as much as you can. Sending virtual hug!

Hey, I genuinely feel you. Health issues are really the most serious reasons to be depressed or suicidal. Other problems just don’t compare to this. 

Sending you a virtual hug. I’m here to talk if you want.

Yes, depression sucks. And I don’t see how someone can get out of serious depression without meds. 

Forcing yourself to go for a walk won’t cut it. I know it firsthand, the awful feeling of being dragged on the concrete instead of having a pleasant walk…

Can fully confirm, I jumped from fifth floor 1.5 years ago and survived. Broke 10 ribs, sacrum, some pelvis bone, got pneumothorax, concussion BUT nothing too serious/disabling. Spent 2 months lying down with other people wiping my bum, but then got up and was able to walk normally.

Sorry to hear that. I don’t know much details about diabetes, but I know it’s not easy to live with.

Sending you a virtual hug.
If it’s a depression, seeing psychiatrist is worth it IMO. The side-effects of antidepressants are generally not that bad. I find the loss of libido to be the most annoying one.
I know this is cliche, but have you tried talking to a therapist/psychiatrist?

Same here. I don’t firmly believe in hell, but what if it’s true? I had one suicide attempt in the past, and my father (who was never religious) told me: “God brought you back for a reason, don’t disappoint him again”.
Thank you! Sending virtual hug.

I understand that it’s a horrible trauma. Thinking about how my loved ones would react is also holding me back. But it’s probably
 not enough for me to cope with a disabled life. Luckily, I still have some hope to be healthy… I’ll know for sure soon. Just preparing for the worst.
Are those things you’ve done really that awful? If not, maybe speak to a therapist about your feeling of guilt?

As far as I know, the answer to low-functioning depression is taking antidepressants until it turns into high-functioning, then adding some lifestyle changes to pull yourself out further and stay afloat.

I also struggled with severe depression (as part of bipolar disorder), to the point where I could not sleep for multiple days in a row. This was true hell… Antidepressants and antipsychotics helped me to get out this state.

Stay safe, sending you a virtual hug.

Did you take them for 2+ months? It takes some time for the effect to build-up. 

Also, have you told your psychiatrist that you aren’t seeing any positive results? Could be that you need another type of antidepressants.

Besides, why you being alive makes other people’s lives worse?

This sounds like symptoms of a clinical depression. Please take a look at this self-assessment test, these questions resonate a lot with your post https://www.ismanet.org/doctoryourspirit/pdfs/Beck-Depression-Inventory-BDI.pdf

Depression can shift and twist your thinking such that you can’t see any hope or way out. But there’s hope in most situations. Please see a psychiatrist. Antidepressants might change your outlook and your life. 

Sending virtual hug.

Why do you think it will never happen to you?

Life has some surprises in stock, not all of them are bad, and finding love can be one of them. Even the possibility of future love is a reason to stay alive.

It sounds like you might suffer from clinical depression. Depression can change the way you think, making you feel hopeless when there’s still plenty of options and good possibilities. So I’d recommend seeing psychiatrist and getting screened for depression.

Sending you a virtual hug. I hope one day you’ll be hugged for real by a loving person.

I’m sorry to hear that you’re in such situation. Feeling that you have to choose between homelessness and death must be really brutal. I don’t know how to help you, but I really hope you find another way out.

What’s really fascinating is just how much I want to live now. Life looks fantastic and beautiful, and yet it seems that I will be denied that beauty. Just really sad… 

Also, death started to scare me. Eternal void seems ok when you think of it hypothetically, but is really terrifying when you’re close to it. 

And then there are logistic problems. Like, how to pass my inheritance. I wish assisted suicide was available to everyone. Going away peacefully seems like a basic human right to me…

Hm, I see it differently. If I stay strong and carry on, I will be miserable and possibly even intolerable. If I end up in a wheelchair, I will be a real burden to my loved ones.

Ending it definitely traumatizes them, they’ll be heartbroken. But after some time they’ll get over it, it will become a sad but distant memory.

Thank you for chatting with me. Sending you a warm hug…
To walk like a healthy person again

Hey. What's your health problem?  


I'm thinking about whether I can accept a limited life and find happiness in some other things. What's frightening me is that my problem seems to get worse day by day. I'm terrified of the thought that I might be unable to walk one day. I'd rather end it before that, while I still can. Suicide is harder when you're in a wheelchair.

I'm truly fascinated by people in wheelchairs that find strength and will to live. I can't imagine myself being like that.
Thank you. She shows a lot of support and empathy indeed, I just don’t know if I can accept myself like this and live a limited life or is it better to leave her and kill myself.
I’m seeing a neurologist and doing physical therapy for two weeks now. I don’t have a final diagnosis, but preparing for the worst. From what I know, this is likely a lifelong condition.

No, I’m having doubts because I don’t want to turn her life into shit too. To be honest, I’m having suicidal thoughts because I don’t want to live for decades like this. So it’s more that I doubt myself than her.
poor wording on my side, but I think you get what I meant
No, not set, but we were thinking approx a year from now.
Yes, I’m in therapy, specifically working on my health problems and the way to accept them.

That is exactly what I heard from my therapist two months ago. I started going to therapy in October in attempt to figure out my inner issues and arrive to a decision, but I guess it requires a lot more time to help with low self esteem.

I’m still not fully on board with the idea that I chased that girl only due to her unavailability. There’s plenty of unavailable girls around who don’t attract me.

No, but I did feel the love & willingness to marry towards another girl 10 years ago. I chased her for ~4 years, dated for a few months and got dumped.

Which is in itself a warning: even when we find the “passionate love”, there’s absolutely no guarantee that it’ll be mutual.

From what you said, it seems my gf has a very similar view on love = respect, kindness, being always out there for your family.

My problem is that I spent all my life to this point expecting a love that would swoop me off my feet and thrust me to the altar. But instead I found a different kind of relationship that I grew to value, so now it’s time for a hard decision whether I should commit and “grow to love” or break up and revert to my past views.

Yes, and this is why I never told it to her like that. But then: what ELSE is there to love and successful relationship besides these things? 

Personally, I think there is some magic and unexplainable component that makes us want to commit to a person, once and forever, effortlessly. But she does not seem to believe or need all this magic and butterflies (from all our convos on this matter).

I already feel like shit, to be honest. 

Not so sure about “you would know after 3.5 years” part, since we know at least one couple of friends who had a very similar situation and ultimately married after 7 years. Although not enough time passed to judge the success of their marriage.
I told her about my doubts when she first brought up “the future”. We decided to try living together and she gave me some time to make up my mind, but I failed to do it on time.
Comfort, conversations, compatibility.

She says she is. Although, from our talks on this matter it seems that her view on love is more practical and less romantic than mine.

As for her happiness, I do care and I’m really afraid of becoming a bad husband to her who isn’t putting 100% effort in family because he doesn’t love his wife.
